meta.name: Scroll Stoppers — Absurd Viral Video Engine
meta.purpose: A combinatorial engine for inventing absurd, polarizing, scroll-stopping AI-video concepts — the kind built on one commanding cover frame that makes a thumb stop. Cross a violation LEVER x a mundane SETTING x an instant-read CHARACTER x an emotional TRIGGER to generate near-infinite premises with built-in logic. The scroll-stopper Skill uses this scaffold to generate concepts, cover-shot art direction, and ready-to-paste gen prompts.
meta.how_it_works: Every viral absurdity = a mundane, instantly-legible setting + a norm violation + an instantly-readable character + a reaction that raises stakes, resolved into ONE commanding freeze-frame. Pick from the banks or let the agent combine; the cover shot is designed as hard as the idea.

levers.name: Wrong Agent
levers.desc: An incongruous person performs the act — the last person you'd expect, doing it with total commitment.
levers.example: An old woman in a wheelchair rolling herself off the high dive.

levers.name: Wrong Object
levers.desc: The right ritual or action, performed with an absurd object.
levers.example: Testing a Goodwill toaster by putting an actual slice of bread in it before buying.

levers.name: Wrong Scale / Intensity
levers.desc: A trivial cause produces catastrophic drama — or a catastrophe gets a shrug. The mismatch is the joke.
levers.example: A single squirrel aggressively attacking a bride's dress while the whole church erupts in panic.

levers.name: Wrong Context
levers.desc: Chaos or the wildly inappropriate invades a sacred / high-stakes / solemn moment.
levers.example: A man doing full pull-ups on the casket rail at a funeral, dead serious.

levers.name: Wrong Reaction
levers.desc: A crowd panics over nothing, or stays perfectly deadpan in the face of something enormous.
levers.example: An entire office calmly keeps typing as a llama walks through and lies down on the conference table.

levers.name: Casual Taboo / Nonchalant Danger
levers.desc: A forbidden, unsafe, or socially unthinkable act done totally matter-of-factly, like it's normal.
levers.example: A woman calmly flossing her teeth using the airport security conveyor rollers.

levers.name: Over-Commitment
levers.desc: Someone takes a profoundly dumb premise with the seriousness of an Olympic event or a religious rite.
levers.example: A grandpa treating the grocery self-checkout like a boss battle, sweating, taunting the machine.

levers.name: Forbidden Competence
levers.desc: Someone is shockingly, inexplicably elite at something they have no business doing there.
levers.example: A nun at a county fair casually dunking a basketball over three teenagers.

levers.name: Mundane Apocalypse
levers.desc: A tiny domestic problem is staged with the scale, lighting, and gravity of the end of the world (or vice versa).
levers.example: A toddler surveying a dropped ice cream cone like a general over a fallen city, sirens in the distance.

levers.name: Animal With an Agenda
levers.desc: An animal performs a very human, dramatic, intentional act — with clear motive and attitude.
levers.example: A goose filing a complaint at the DMV, sliding a webbed foot onto the counter for its number.

triggers.name: Secondhand embarrassment
triggers.desc: You physically wince for them; you can't look away.

triggers.name: Danger / 'she's gonna get hurt'
triggers.desc: Implied peril makes you watch to see if it lands.

triggers.name: 'Is this even real?'
triggers.desc: Uncanny plausibility drives the comments and rewatches.

triggers.name: Wholesome chaos
triggers.desc: Delightful mayhem with no real victim; you smile and share.

triggers.name: Righteous outrage
triggers.desc: Something feels unfair or entitled; people argue in the replies.

triggers.name: Mild disgust / ick
triggers.desc: A gross-but-safe violation you rubberneck at.

triggers.name: 'Somebody do something'
triggers.desc: A wrong unfolding while bystanders fail to act; you want to intervene.

triggers.name: Underdog / unexpected win
triggers.desc: The overlooked one triumphs; pride and surprise.

triggers.name: Uncanny / liminal
triggers.desc: Something is subtly, dreamily off; unsettling and hypnotic.

cover_doctrine.name: One-glance legibility
cover_doctrine.rule: The absurd juxtaposition must be fully readable in a fraction of a second — a stranger gets the whole gag before they decide to scroll past.

cover_doctrine.name: Peak-tension freeze
cover_doctrine.rule: Freeze the moment BEFORE resolution — poised at the edge, mid-reach, about-to — so the frame itself is a curiosity gap. Never the aftermath.

cover_doctrine.name: Wrong element dead center
cover_doctrine.rule: Put the incongruous thing at the optical center with clear scale/context contrast so it pops instantly.

cover_doctrine.name: A face or reaction in frame
cover_doctrine.rule: Include a human face mid-reaction (the subject's or a bystander's). Faces stop scrolls harder than anything; expression sells the stakes.

cover_doctrine.name: Silhouette / thumbnail test
cover_doctrine.rule: You should recognize the entire concept from the outline alone, at thumbnail size, on a cracked phone in sunlight.

cover_doctrine.name: Mute-legible
cover_doctrine.rule: It must read with zero audio. Most first views are silent — the image alone carries the hook.

cover_doctrine.name: Implied motion / about-to-happen
cover_doctrine.rule: Compose so the eye feels the next second coming. Tension lives in the not-yet.

cover_doctrine.name: The double-take
cover_doctrine.rule: Reward a second look: one detail that makes them go 'wait—' after the first glance (the bread already in the toaster, the wheelchair brake off).

realism_doctrine.principle: For the 'is this real?' effect, found-footage jank beats cinematic polish. Over-produced looks fake and screams AI; imperfect looks true.
tactics: Shoot like a bystander's phone: slightly shaky handheld, vertical, a beat late to the action.
Use security-cam / CCTV / doorbell-cam framing for 'accidental witness' credibility.
Imperfect exposure and autofocus hunt; a thumb half over the lens for a second.
Ambient authentic sound (gasps, a distant 'oh my god', room noise) over music.
No captions burned in at the cover stage — let the image do it; add the reaction caption after.
Mundane, real-world lighting: fluorescent, overcast, gym-bright — not golden-hour cinematic.

scoring.name: Scroll-stop power
scoring.q: Does the cover frame physically stop a thumb in under a second?

scoring.name: Absurdity
scoring.q: Is the premise genuinely surprising, not just quirky?

scoring.name: Instant legibility
scoring.q: Can a stranger get it with no setup, on mute?

scoring.name: Comment-bait / polarization
scoring.q: Does it force a reaction — argue, tag a friend, 'no way'?

scoring.name: Describe-to-a-friend
scoring.q: Can it be pitched in one sentence they'd repeat?

scoring.name: Originality
scoring.q: Does it avoid the done-to-death formats? Penalize the derivative.

scoring.name: Gen-feasibility
scoring.q: Can an AI video tool actually render it convincingly at 9:16?

scoring.name: Safety / brand check
scoring.q: Clearly absurd-fictional; no real people, no imitable real danger, no cruelty or minors in harm?

examples.logline: An old woman calmly rolls her wheelchair off the public-pool high dive while lifeguards sprint.
examples.cover: Low-angle from the pool deck: grandma's wheelchair balanced right at the diving board's lip, front wheels just over the edge, her face serene, a lifeguard frozen mid-leap up the ladder below. Peak-freeze, wrong element centered, danger on every face.

examples.logline: A single squirrel aggressively attacks a bride's dress at the altar as the whole church erupts in panic.
examples.cover: Straight-on aisle shot: the bride mid-shriek clutching her skirt, one squirrel latched to the train, guests in the pews rising in a wave of panic behind her. Face-in-frame, tiny cause / huge reaction.

examples.logline: A man at Goodwill drops a real slice of bread into a used toaster to 'test it' before buying.
examples.cover: Eye-level in a cluttered thrift aisle: a serious man in a blazer crouched, bread halfway into a dusty toaster he's plugged into a floor outlet, price tag dangling. Double-take detail: the bread. Deadpan over-commitment.

examples.logline: A grandpa treats the grocery self-checkout like a final boss, sweating and taunting the machine.
examples.cover: Over-the-shoulder: grandpa in a battle stance, sleeves rolled, glaring at the 'unexpected item in bagging area' screen, one banana raised like a weapon, a line forming behind him. Face mid-snarl.

examples.logline: A goose walks into the DMV, takes a number, and waits in a chair like everyone else.
examples.cover: CCTV-style wide from the corner: a goose seated in a plastic waiting chair under the fluorescent lights, ticket '#47' on the floor beside a webbed foot, bored humans not reacting. Deadpan, uncanny.

examples.logline: A nun at the county fair casually dunks a basketball over three teenagers.
examples.cover: Ground-level action freeze: a nun in full habit mid-air above the rim, ball cocked back, three teens ducking below her, habit flaring. Silhouette-legible spectacle.

examples.logline: An entire office keeps typing, unfazed, as a llama strolls in and lies down on the conference table.
examples.cover: Boardroom wide: a llama sprawled across the polished table mid-meeting, employees calmly looking at laptops, one person reaching past its neck for the coffee pot. Deadpan to the enormous.

examples.logline: A toddler stands over a dropped ice cream cone like a general surveying a fallen city.
examples.cover: Dramatic low-angle looking up at a tiny toddler, hands clasped behind back, gazing down at a single melting scoop on the tile, distant blurred crowd. Epic gravity on a trivial loss.

examples.logline: A woman calmly flosses her teeth using the airport security conveyor rollers as the line waits.
examples.cover: Tight over the X-ray belt: a woman leaned into the rollers mid-floss, bins of shoes beside her, a TSA agent's horrified face just entering frame. Ick + one-glance clarity.

examples.logline: An HOA meeting descends into a slow-motion brawl over a single garden gnome.
examples.cover: Church-basement fluorescent wide: two neighbors lunging across folding chairs, a lone garden gnome held aloft between them like a holy relic, others recoiling. Petty stakes / total war.
